references.text: John the Baptist bears the same witness earlier in the chapter: "After me comes a man who has come before me, for he was before me" ([ref:Joh 1:15|John 1:15]). Verse 30 repeats this testimony almost word for word.

John the Baptist points to the one who "comes after me," and whom he is not worthy to untie the sandal strap of ([ref:Joh 1:27|John 1:27]). This is part of the same testimony concerning Jesus' preeminence.

Jesus' preexistence as the Word – "In the beginning was the Word" – is the basis for the statement "he was before me" ([ref:Joh 1:1-2|John 1:1-2]). Although John the Baptist was born before Jesus, Christ existed from eternity.
Jesus himself confirms his preexistence with the words "Before Abraham was, I am" ([ref:Joh 8:58|John 8:58]), which supports John the Baptist's testimony that Jesus "was before" him.
In his high priestly prayer, Jesus speaks of the glory he had with the Father "before the world existed" ([ref:Joh 17:5|John 17:5]), confirming his eternal preeminence.
Paul expresses the same truth: "He is before all things, and in him all things hold together" ([ref:Kol 1:17|Colossians 1:17]). Christ is before everything created, including John the Baptist.

The prophecy about the ruler from Bethlehem says that "his origin is from of old, from ancient days" ([ref:Mi 5:1|Micah 5:1]). This points to the Messiah's preexistence, which John the Baptist testifies to.

Also in Matthew, John the Baptist testifies that "the one who comes after me is stronger than I am" ([ref:Matt 3:11|Matthew 3:11]). It is the same testimony concerning Jesus' superiority and preeminence.
In Luke, John the Baptist likewise says that "there comes one who is stronger than I am" ([ref:Luk 3:16|Luke 3:16]), a parallel to the testimony in John 1:30.
Mark recounts John the Baptist's testimony: "After me comes the one who is stronger than I am" ([ref:Mark 1:7|Mark 1:7]), showing that this testimony is preserved in all four Gospels.
